equivalent: `EHarris::new` builds its `SAE` with `TimeSurface::new(geom, Decay::Linear { window_s }, false)` — `split` is FALSE, which is the detector's own documented choice ('the detector is looking for geometry, and splitting the planes here would halve the pattern an alternating edge writes'). With `split == false`, `TimeSurface::last_time` computes `let plane = if self.split { .. } else { 0 }`, so the polarity argument is discarded before it reaches the buffer and both `On` and `Off` read index `0 * pixels + idx`. equivalent: The Harris response is invariant under transposing its patch, so this mutation changes no observable output. `GY` is exactly the transpose of `GX` (`GX[dj][di] == GY[di][dj]` entry for entry), so evaluating the pair on a transposed image gives `gx' (i, j) = gy (j, i)` and `gy' (i, j) = gx (j, i)`. Summing over the full square interior then gives `Mxx' = Myy`, `Myy' = Mxx` and `Mxy' = sum gy*gx = Mxy`, and the score `det - k*trace^2 = Mxx*Myy - Mxy^2 - k*(Mxx + Myy)^2` is symmetric in `Mxx` and `Myy`, so it is unchanged. The module already asserts this invariance directly in `swapping_the_sobel_kernels_is_an_equivalent_mutation`, which is the same algebra reached from the other side.

label: the rotating bar's cap is ten times what its doc states
the rotating bar stops one crossing short of the duration
equivalent: Equivalent under the closed form the function documents; the slot it gives up is margin, not reach. Write p = period, D = duration, n = floor(D/p) and u = -base/p for one pixel. The crossings the doc names are `t_k = base + k*p` with `0 <= t_k <= D`, i.e. k from `ceil(u)` to `floor(u + D/p)`, and there are at most `floor(u + D/p) - ceil(u) + 1 <= floor(D/p) + 1 = n + 1` of them, because `floor(a + b) <= floor(a) + ceil(b)` for all reals (equality when b is an integer, otherwise `floor(a+b) <= floor(a)+floor(b)+1 = floor(a)+ceil(b)`). The mutant starts at the same `k0 = ceil(u)` and has exactly `n + 1` slots, so it still reaches every admissible k; the slot it drops could only have held `k = ceil(u) + n + 1`, whose time is `t_ceil(u) + (n+1)*p >= (n+1)*p > D` and which the original's own `if t > duration { break }` discards. Measured: 3,591 randomly drawn parameter sets -- omega over eight decades (1e-2 to 1e6), theta0 up to 1e12, four sensor sizes, integer and half-integer centres, durations from 1e-6 s to 10 s -- emitted identical event sets under both (scratch/sweeps_probe.py). What I found and deliberately did not build a test on: the margin becomes observable only where `phi - theta0` has lost the pixel's own angle to rounding, |theta0| around 1e13 and up, so that `base + k0*p` -- a cancellation of two numbers of order |base| -- can land a few ulp below zero and consume a slot the `t >= 0.0` filter then discards. In 200,000 draws that happened 26 times at |theta0| <= 1e14 and 3,394 times at |theta0| <= 1e16. But in that regime the UNMUTATED generator is already outside its own closed form: in 17,779 of 300,000 draws (5.9%) the set it emits is not `{t_k in [0, D]}` evaluated in the same binary64, because the rounding is larger than the margin. A test built on one of the surviving points would pin the rounding of `atan2` and of one cancellation rather than the claim, and would stop distinguishing anything on a libm that rounds `atan2` differently. The module already treats this class of precision loss as a fact about the arithmetic rather than a defect -- see `a_time_surface_seeded_late_loses_precision_to_the_subtraction`, which is the same subtraction. The claim itself is now pinned for a well-conditioned fixture by the new `every_crossing_the_rotating_bars_closed_form_names_is_emitted_and_no_other`, which compares all 226 annulus pixels' emitted times, value for value, against `base + k*period` scanned two slots past each end.

label: the rotating bar's first crossing is taken below zero rather than at or after it
equivalent: Equivalent under the closed form the function documents, by the same counting argument as `the rotating bar stops one crossing short of the duration` (see that entry for the algebra and the measurements). `floor(u)` differs from `ceil(u)` only when u is not an integer, and then it is `ceil(u) - 1`, so the mutant's first slot holds `t_ceil(u) - p`, which lies in [-p, 0) and is discarded by the `if t >= 0.0` filter. That leaves it `n + 1` useful slots out of `n + 2`, and `n + 1` is exactly the bound on how many crossings a pixel can have inside [0, D] -- so it still reaches every one of them. Emitted sets were identical across the same 3,591 drawn parameter sets. This mutation is even harder to make visible than its twin: it additionally needs u to fall just below an integer, and exactly one draw in 300,000 in the rounding-dominated regime both left the unmutated generator agreeing with its own closed form and made this mutant disagree.
